content.text:
ANSWER: The function is `secret_kind(text: &str) -> Option<&'static str>` in `src/memory/guard.rs` (line 53). It first checks the text against the named credential regexes in the `SECRETS` list. These cover private keys, AWS keys, GitHub tokens, `sk-` API keys, Slack tokens, Google API keys, Stripe keys, npm tokens, crates.io tokens, JWTs, credentials in URLs, and `password=`-style assignments. If none match, it uses the `LONG_TOKEN` regex (`[A-Za-z0-9+/_=-]{32,}`) to find long tokens. It reports `"high-entropy token"` if any of those tokens passes the helper `looks_random` (line 62).

`looks_random(token: &str) -> bool`, also in `src/memory/guard.rs`, is the helper that separates random-looking tokens from hashes and ids. It returns false unless the token has lowercase, uppercase and digit characters. It then computes the Shannon entropy of the token's bytes and returns true only if the entropy is above 4.2. Hex hashes and base32 ids are rejected because they can't reach that entropy or lack mixed case. Base64-style keys pass.

`secret_kind` is called by `check_secret` (line 106), which `check` (line 133) calls on the memory text. `check_secret` builds the `Refused` error ("refused: the text looks like a credential (…)"). `check` is called from the `remember` write path in `src/memory/write.rs`. I didn't open `write.rs`, so that last link comes from the search result, not from the code.

CONFIDENCE: high
